videos.description: In this video, we'll explain MCP Clients. ## What is an MCP Client?  **An MCP Client is the bridge that allows a LLM  to break out of its "box" and connect with external tools in real time.** Think of it as a universal translator that allows AI to talk to APIs, databases, financial tools, and web services.  ## What we'll see in this video **This project demonstrates how to build a complete MCP Client** that transforms LLN from a basic chatbot into a **professional financial assistant** capable of:  - 📊 **Analyzing stocks in real time** using 8+ technical indicators (MACD, Bollinger, RSI, Fibonacci) - 🔍 **Searching for information on Google** and automatically processing web content - 📄 **Generating professional reports** in Word and PDF from data analysis - 🤖 **Intelligently orchestrating multiple tools** based on context  ## The Magic of the MCP Protocol  **MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard that makes this possible.** Instead a LLM just "talking," he can now "act": - Calling Yahoo Finance APIs to retrieve stock data - Running complex technical analysis calculations - Creating structured documents with results - Maintaining context across multiple trades  **The result: The LLM goes from being A chat to become a complete financial analyst who can research, calculate, analyse, and report—all in a natural Language.**  We'll create an MCP client that connects in conversational chatbot mode to two MCP servers, one written in Python and the other in JavaScript. videos.title: LLMOps: MCP. Introduction and example in Python. MCP Client and Server #machinelearning #datascience
videos.description: In this video, we will explain what MCP is and provide a practical example of creating an MCP server and interacting with a Python client in chatbot mode.  The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard developed by Anthropic in late 2024 that functions as a "USB-C port for AI applications," providing a standardized way for artificial intelligence models to connect with external data sources, tools, and systems. MCP solves the "MxN" integration problem by transforming it into an "M+N" problem, allowing any AI model to interact with any tool or data source through a common protocol, without the need to develop custom integrations for each combination. This approach has gained rapid adoption by companies such as Block (Square), Apollo, Replit, and Sourcegraph, with over 1,000 MCP servers built by the community by early 2025.  ## The Basics of MCP  MCP emerged as a response to a fundamental limitation of language models: while powerful for generating text, they lack the native ability to interact with the outside world. Before MCP, each integration between an AI model and an external tool required custom development, creating a scaling problem when multiple models needed to connect with multiple tools.  The MCP architecture is composed of three main elements:  1. **MCP Host**: The application where the AI ​​model runs (such as Claude Desktop, IDEs, or enterprise tools). 2. **MCP Client**: Components that maintain connections to MCP servers. 3. **MCP Server**: Lightweight programs that expose specific capabilities through the standardized MCP protocol.
